lines.en: It’s dark by the time we go outside.
I didn’t realize how much time had passed...but I guess it always gets dark a little earlier in the winter.
Kumon-mi, despite being incredibly different from everywhere else in more ways than you can count, is no exception to that.
I silently follow Io as she rounds the corner and heads for whatever bench she normally spends her breaks on, noticing with each hundred feet or so that her disappointment is slowly fading.
Like she’s hitting a different stage of life each time she passes under a streetlight, each one bringing with it a brand new, but instinctively reserved outlook on life as we know it.
The word “caterpillar” comes to mind.
But it’s not the first time I’ve thought of her as something like that.
Something absolutely worthless, but with so much room to grow and so much left to give, if she ever elects to give anything to anyone.
Anyone other than me, I mean.
I’ve already managed to win her over simply by being in the right place at the right time.
But who’s to say that our encounter was the last place or the last time.
For all I know, someone else could swoop in and take her away the second they seem more valuable or even make her seem more valuable.
The two of us have a lot in common.
We’ve accepted our worthlessness and rely on others to make up for what we can’t cultivate within ourselves.
Our blood is poisoned and our minds are tainted.
And while Io has an entire pharmacy’s worth of pills at her bedside to counteract this-
I have these thoughts.
But that’s all I need.
Because everything is going to work out.
Because life will repeat itself and mistakes will correct themselves.
Either that or I disappear.
I can’t lose.
I’d definitely prefer not disappearing, though.
And for Io’s sake, temporary or not, I’m going to continue hoping that doesn’t happen.
: Here.
Io props herself onto the edge of a park bench, dragging her knees to her chest and shivering as a gust of wind comes to greet us.
I sit next to her and place my unnamed wooden robot down on the opposite end.
A minute or two goes by without any dialogue...but this is fine.
I expected this.
Any minute now, she’ll revert back to her instinctive self-deprecation.
: I really suck, don’t I?
See?
: Why? Because you had a sensible reaction to someone insulting something you worked really hard on?
: Because I dragged you down with me.
: Those girls are going to remember this.
: You're probably going to have to explain yourself to them now.
: All I did was create more problems for you.
: Which means I suck.
: I don’t see it as much of a problem.
: Noriko will probably get jealous and Kirin will probably just accuse me of sleeping with you or something.
: Yeah...
: Not going to lie, that sounds like a pretty big problem.
: I think it would be more of a problem for you than it would be for me. No one really thinks highly of me to begin with.
: I think highly of you.
: It’s not a problem for me since I don’t talk to any of them. They can think whatever they want.
: Yeah, I guess it’s kind of hard to be ostracized when you’re already a wallflower.
: I suck at being a wallflower too. I couldn’t even win the wallflower contest thing for the dorm war.
: I’m pretty sure not winning makes you a better wallflower.
: Hmm...maybe.
: Yumi seems to be actively hated, though. While everyone probably looks at me and thinks, “Oh, right. She’s in this class.”
: So I guess I’m in my own category when you look at things that way.
: You’re definitely one of a kind. I’ll give you that.
: You know...
: You know, I'm sorry for saying this again out of what seems like nowhere...
: But I really think you should break up with that gyaru girl.
: The one that you’re well aware I’m not actually dating?
: I’m not well aware of that. I still think it’s technically possible that you’re lying.
: Well, I’m not really sure what else I can do to prove to you that I’m not.
: You coooooould...start dating me instead?
: I think that might help prove it.
: Two minutes ago, you were talking about how just following you would create problems for me...and now you’re suggesting we start dating.
: Because I know you won't want to.
: And you would?
: I’ve gotta say, you don’t really seem like the type to start any sort of “official” relationship with anyone.
: It’s not really something I’ve ever wanted...that’s true.
: But I think it would be kind of nice if it were you.
: It’d be really hard, though.
: Why’s that?
: Because I’d cry a lot.
: And probably freak out on you over a bunch of different things that aren’t your fault or that you can’t control.
: Oh, and I have lots of medications that you would probably have to help me pay for.
: And I’d be up all hours of the night banging on stuff when I’m making shelves and dressers and other furniture for Uta.
: So we’re moving in together, too?
: I move quickly.
: Well, that’s not entirely true.
: In some areas I move quickly. In other areas, I’d rather not move at all.
: Yeah, this relationship is already exhausting me and it doesn’t even exist.
: Can I hold your hand?
: Sure. But the second you start calling yourself my girlfriend, I am walking away.
: I can not make that same mistake twice.
: That was all rhetorical. I know I’m not your girlfriend. And I know I’ll probably never be your girlfriend because there are a million better choices and-
: Just give me your hand already.
: Oh, yeah. Sure. Sorry.
: Don’t apologize. Just accept that this is a momentary sign of affection and that it does not mean we are formally dating.
: I accept your affection and henceforth agree to not enter into a relationship with you.
: But if you change your mind...you can have me.
: What kind of “have” are we talking about here? Because that word carries some rather heavy connotations in my dictionary.
: It means that you get to inherit Io Ichimonji and her six billion pounds of baggage.
: And that you need to figure out what to do about it because she’s been trying for years and has solved absolutely nothing.
: This isn’t even high maintenance in the lowest way possible anymore. It’s just high maintenance.
: True. But how many other girlfriends could you get right now that could build you a fence?
: I’m sure that line would kill in a dating profile.
: Online dating is stupid. Whatever happened to traditional relationships that formed from just...people meeting each other out in public and stuff?
: Half of them ended in divorce.
: Oh. Right. That’s a thing.
: Do you think I’m crazy, Sensei?
: I think neurotic is probably a better word.
: I think that’s fair.
: I know better than anyone how much of a handful I can be.
: Thankfully, your hands are really big. And surprisingly soft.
: Have you been using our new scented lotion?
: I’m surprised you can feel anything with the amount of calluses on your hands.
: Hey! You already know I’m kind of self-conscious about that!
: Does this mean I should let go?
: No! I’ve never held hands with a boy before. I like it.
: Have you held hands with a girl?
: I mean...not that I can remember. But I’m sure I’ve held hands with Uta at least once.
: Are you two actually closer than you look?
: Are you about to make this weird?
: Making things weird is basically the only way I know how to function in extended conversations.
: Why else would I bring up sex so much?
: Because you're trying to groom everybody.
: Ow! Hey! Why are you squeezing me?!
: Sorry. Just a reflex.
: Geez...
: To think a hand this soft could crush mine with almost zero effort...
: I bet you wish you had one of your four boxcutters on you now, huh?
: As if I’d ever go out of my way to hurt you.
: If I was truly attempting to crush your appendages, I really hope you would hurt me.
: If you ever try to crush any part of me, I'll probably deserve it.
: I don’t think there’s much a person can do to deserve something like that.
: I do.
: What a quick response.
: Quick and easy.
: Like sex.
: You’re making things weird again.
: The conversation’s been going on for a while.
: Do you want it to stop? Are you already tired of me?
: Not really. But I can’t imagine you’re allowed to stay on break for this long.
: Did you actually think this was my break and that I wasn't just running away because I was about to have a panic attack?
: I mean...it could have been both.
: I guess it could have.
: I’m feeling a lot better now, though.
: And I’m sure it goes without saying, but I’m glad you followed me out. Even if it seemed like I might have been trying to push you away.
: That’s gonna happen a lot from now on, you know? Times where I say the opposite of how I feel because I’m scared or nervous.
: Are you okay with that?
: It doesn’t sound like I have much of a choice.
: You do, though. You can abandon me whenever you want and I can’t do anything about it.
: I’m definitely at the point where that would really mess me up, though. So...sorry to put all of that pressure on you again.
: I’m getting used to it.
: Would you like a reward for all of your hard work?
: I already got a robot.
: Would you like another robot?
: How about an Io?
: You already have an Io.
: An Io I wouldn’t mind being closer with.
: But you already said you don’t want to date me.
: And that’s not what I’m saying now...
: Then...you...
: I think I know what you’re saying, but...
: I’m just messing around.
: Yeah. Yeah, I know.
: Sorry, it’s just...
: I know it’s not much, but...you can at least hold my hand like this whenever you want...
: Like, even if it’s in class or something. I’m okay with it.
: But...anything more right now is...
: Why are you giving me a whole explanation? Just tell me to shut up if I say something you don’t like.
: You just...sounded really serious when you...insinuated that.
: And I don’t want you to get your hopes up and then get fed up with me if I take too long to do what you want and-
: Shut up.
: Okay.
: You wouldn’t want me anyway. I’m too scrawny and my hands are all hard. And I have stupid hair.
: Your hair isn’t stupid.
: You directly told me my hair was stupid once and I still haven’t lived it down.
: Stop taking all of my jokes so seriously.
: Stop saying everything with the exact same inflection then. It’s hard to keep up.
: Welcome to my life. Everything about you is hard to keep up with.
: Everyone and everything else, too.
: The world moves too quickly.
: And in other areas, it doesn’t move at all.
: I like you, by the way.
: I’m sure I’ve made that pretty obvious. But I feel like now is a really good time to come out and just say it.
: I had a feeling.
: Like, a lot.
: My heart is beating like crazy right now.
: It’s keeping me warm even though it’s like negative a million degrees outside.
: Why are you telling me this when you know I’m not going to date you?
: Because now you’ll have no choice but to think about it.
: If I didn’t tell you, you’d probably walk home whispering some weird monologue to yourself about how I’m lost or you’re lost-
: But now you’ll just think about my stupid hair and my garbage robot and how dating me would be harder than adopting six babies all at once.
: You really need to work on selling yourself a little better.
: Sorry. I only sell products I’d be fine with using myself.
: Have I mentioned our new scented lotion?
: Ah! You’re squeezing again!
: You’ve said “scented lotion” way too many times today.
: At least...take a free sample!
: Sensei! Stop!
The two of us head back to the bathhouse and I drop Io off without going inside.
There’s a distinct lack of inner monologue on my way home after that.
But there are plenty of thoughts about a girl with stupid hair.
Io’s affection has increased to [io_love]!
